body.name: \mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)
body.construction: For \(c\in[1/4,3/4]\) and \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), \(\mathcal Q(c,\vartheta)=\{q=(q_{d,y})_{d,y\in\{0,1\}}:\ q_{d,y}:[0,1]\to[0,1]\text{ is measurable},\ \sum_{d,y}q_{d,y}(x)=1\text{ for Lebesgue-almost every }x,\text{ the two margins are restrictions of separate one-sided radius-}M\text{, order-}s\text{ H\"older extensions split at }c,\ \Delta q_D(c)\in[\kappa_n,2\kappa_n],\ \Delta q_Y(c)=\vartheta\Delta q_D(c)\}\). The coordinate \(q_{1,1}(x)\) is otherwise free over its binary Fr\'echet interval, so zero and singular cells belong to the domain.
